rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses returned after completing the forty days—Dhu al-Qadah and ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah—and received the inscribed Torah tablets, reportedly comprising a thousand surahs of a thousand verses each and borne by seventy camels.
rows.anchor: بعدما استوفى الأربعين ذا القعدة وعشر ذي الحجة وأخذ الألواح المكتوب فيها التوراة وكانت ألف سورة كل سورة ألف آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غضبان means angry, while أسفا describes intense sorrow over their deed or intense anger.
rows.anchor: أي : شديد الحزن على ما فعلوا أو شديد الغضب ومنه قوله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الإمام الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says asaf can combine sorrow and anger, though the word may denote either feeling separately.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام الراغب الأسف الحزن والغضب معا

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A saying attributed to the Prophet calls sudden death mercy for believers and a seizure for unbelievers.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام في موت الفجأة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi pictures Moses arriving amid the people’s noise as they beat tambourines around the calf and danced, then rebuking them.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (ون بميان قوم رسيد بانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good promise was God’s truthful promise of the Torah, containing light and guidance, which they could not deny.
rows.anchor: بأن يعطيكم التوراة فيها ما فيها من النور والهدى

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Bahr al-ʿUlum reads hasanan as supremely good: no promise is more beautiful than the Torah’s guidance and light.
rows.anchor: متناهيا في الحسن فإنه تعالى وعدهم أن يعطيهم التوراة التي فيها هدى ونور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishari lesson: fulfillment of a good divine promise can itself become a trial, as the Torah and Moses’s meeting with God preceded the calf’s worship; this good trial ended in repentance, deliverance, and raised ranks.
rows.anchor: إذا وعد قوما لا بد له من الوفاء بالوعد فيحتمل أن يكون ذلك الوفاء فتنة للقوم وبلاء لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa links to an unstated proposition, and the interrogative rejects only the attached proposition: perhaps the wait for fulfillment grew long and caused their lapse.
rows.anchor: الفاء للعطف على مقدر والهمزة لإنكار المعطوف ونفيه فقط

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalalayn takes the interval as the time Moses was separated from them.
rows.anchor: مدة مفارقتي إياكم يقال طال عهدي بك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened wrath is great punishment and vengeance from their absolute Lord, incurred by worshipping something proverbial for stupidity.
rows.anchor: عذاب عظيم وانتقام شديد كائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’s appointment was their pledge to remain firm in his commands until he returned; the genitive construction makes the promise their commitment to him.
rows.anchor: وعدكم إياي بالثبات على ما أمرتكم به إلى أن أرجع من الميقات على إضافة المصدر إلى مفعوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final fa follows either branch: they broke the pledge accidentally after forgetting through delay, or deliberately because they wanted wrath to descend.
rows.anchor: كأنه قيل أنسيتم الوعد بطول العهد فاختلفتموه خطأ أم أردتم حلول الغضب عليكم فأخلفتموه عمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadharu means to cast something away because it is scarcely valued; its past form wadhara is unused.
rows.anchor: يقال فلان يذر الشيء أي : يقذفه لقلة اعتداده به ولم يستعمل ماضيه أي : وذر

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus defines qaʿ as level, settled ground from which mountains and hills have opened away.
rows.anchor: قال في "القاموس" القاع أرض سهلة مطمئنة قد انفرجت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safsaf describes a level plain whose parts appear uniform in every direction.
rows.anchor: على صنف واحد من كل جهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vision concerns the mountains’ former places and may be by sight or insight; this independent clause explains the level plain.
rows.anchor: في مقار الجبال لا بالبصر ولا بالبصيرة استئناف مبين لكيفية القاع الصفصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAwajan with kasra is an imperceptible deviation, fitting meanings, whereas the other form concerns what the eye perceives.
rows.anchor: بكسر العين أي : عوجا ما كأنه لغاية خفائه

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat distinguishes visible crookedness, such as upright wood, from deviation grasped by thought and insight, as in religion or livelihood.
rows.anchor: العوج العطف عن حال الانتصاب والعوج يقال فيما يدرك بالبصر كالخشب المنتصب ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amta is even a slight rise.
rows.anchor: يكون في أرض بسيطة وكالدين والمعاش {ولا أمتا} ارتفاعا يسيرا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari defines amta as a small protrusion.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري الأمت النتوء اليسير

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus lists amta as raised ground, small hills, and both depressions and elevations.
rows.anchor: وفي "القاموس" الأمت المكان المرتفع والتلال الصغار

rows.speaker: المناسبات
rows.claim: Al-Munasabat explains the phrase as having no unevenness of elevation and depression.
rows.anchor: قال في "المناسبات" {ولا أمتا} أي : تفاوتا بارتفاع وانخفاض

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalalayn likewise glosses the two terms as neither lowering nor raising of the terrain.
rows.anchor: وفي "الجلالين" {عوجا ولا أمتا} انخفاضا وارتفاعا

rows.speaker: الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Farisi’s Persian gloss also describes the ground as having neither depression nor height.
rows.anchor: ومثله ما في تفسير الفارسي حيث قال : (عوجا ستى دفرمناره ولا امتا ونه بلندى وشته)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time is the day the mountains are pulverized, and it serves as the temporal setting for people following the caller.
rows.anchor: على إضافة اليوم إلى وقت النسف وهو ظرف لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People follow Israfil, who calls them to the gathering at the second trumpet blast while standing on the rock in Jerusalem, summoning decayed bones and scattered limbs to appear before the Merciful.
rows.anchor: وهو إسرافيل عليه السلام يدعو الناس عند النفخة الثانية قائما على صخرة بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrected approach the caller’s direction from every side.
rows.anchor: من كل جانب إلى جهته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No summoned person turns aside from the caller; the even ground offers no obstacle and the sound travels unobstructed.
rows.anchor: لا يعوج له مدعو ولا يعدل عنه بل يستوي إليه من غير انحراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Voices grow low through terror and awe; khushuʿ is submission, humility, and stillness, while the term may apply to sound, sight, or bodily submission.
rows.anchor: خفضت من شدة الفزع وخفتت لهيبته والخشوع الخضوع وهو التواضع والسكون

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat says khushuʿ is usually seen in the limbs, while dharaʿa is usually in the heart; a transmitted saying links a humbled heart to humbled limbs.
rows.anchor: وفي "المفردات" الخشوع ضراعة وأكثر ما يستعمل فيما يوجد على الجوارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound is moving air produced by two bodies colliding; a letter is specifically a human convention.
rows.anchor: والصوت هواء متموج بتصادم جسمين وهو عام والحرف مخصوص بالإنسان وضعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hams is faint sound, as in whispered consonants and the quietest sound of footsteps.
rows.anchor: صوتا خفيا ومنه الحروف المهموسة وهمس الأقدام أخفى ما يكون من صوتها

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi identifies the faint sound as the footsteps of people walking toward the gathering.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (س نشنوى تودران روزمكر آوازى نرم يعنى صوت اقدام ايشان

rows.speaker: الإمام الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali’s eschatological account begins with the first trumpet: mountains fly, rivers burst into one another, stars scatter, the heavens and earth change, and the living die.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام الغزالي في "الدرة الفاخرة" ينفخ في الصور أي : نفخة أولى

rows.speaker: الإمام الغزالي
rows.claim: He continues that a flame from a hidden chamber ignites the seas; the earth becomes black mire and the heavens resemble oil dregs and molten copper.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام الغزالي في "الدرة الفاخرة"

rows.speaker: الإمام الغزالي
rows.claim: A life-giving sea from the Throne rains upon the earth, bodies regrow in their former ages, and a gentle wind leaves the land level.
rows.anchor: ثم يفتح تعالى خزانة من خزائن العرش فيها بحر الحياة فيمطر به الأرض وهو كمني الرجال فتنبت الأجسام

rows.speaker: الإمام الغزالي
rows.claim: God revives Israfil, whose blast at Jerusalem releases souls through the trumpet’s holes to their bodies, including beasts and birds; all emerge onto the surface, also called al-sahira or, by another view, a desert at Hell’s edge.
rows.anchor: ثم يحيى الله تعالى إسرافيل فينفخ من صخرة بيت المقدس فتخرج الأرواح من ثقب في الصور بعددها ويحل كل روح في جسده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes the resurrected land as white silver on which no one has sinned since its creation.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أرض من فضة بيضاء لم يعص الله عليها منذ خلقها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya interpretation takes the earth as free of crookedness because it is purified, and without unevenness at its corners.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : {لا ترى فيها عوجا} من نقاياها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: In the inward reading, the caller is one who called people in worldly life and they answered their own callers.
rows.anchor: الذي دعاهم في الدنيا فأجابوا داعيهم

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Every caller’s hearers respond by their human disposition; ultimately God is both caller and responder, guiding through the tongue of divine will, as in 10:25.
rows.anchor: يعني كل داع من الدعاة يكون مجيبا في جبلته

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Each age has many followers of callers to ego, world, Satan, angel, prophet, Heaven, or nearness, in varying ranks; followers of God’s caller are only exceptional people of God.
rows.anchor: ولهذا السر يوجد في كل زمان من متبعي كل داع خلق عظيم ولا يوجد في كل قرن من متبعي داعي الله إلا الشواذ

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: When God’s compassionate caller summons a person, the voices of all competing callers submit, fall silent, and are cut off.
rows.anchor: إذا دعا عبدا بالرحمانية خشعت وانقادت وذلت أصوات جميع الدعاة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The remaining hams is the invited person’s footsteps as they move toward the caller.
rows.anchor: أي : إلا وطأ أقدام المدعو ونقلها إلى داعيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mathnawi verse warns the reasonable person to follow God’s true caller: worldly and demonic attractions lead to regret, and knowing the end would have prevented pursuit.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يتبع داعي الله الحق فإن ما سواه باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the terrible Day, intercessors will not benefit anyone except those admitted by the exception.
rows.anchor: لا تنفع الشفاعة} من الشفعاء أحدا

rows.speaker: الإمام الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines intercession as joining another to support and plead for them, usually when a higher-ranking person intercedes for a lower one, especially at resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام الراغب الشفاعة الانضمام إلى آخر ناصرا له وسائلا عنه وأكثر ما يستعمل في انضمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only one for whom the Merciful grants permission may be interceded for; permission means notification of approval and leave.
rows.anchor: في أن يشفع له والإذن في الشيء إعلام بإجازته والرخصة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God approves the intercessor’s statement on behalf of that person; others scarcely benefit even if would-be intercessors plead for them, as also stated in 74:48.
rows.anchor: ورضى له قولا} أي : ورضي لأجله قول الشافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, the exception is from the broadest class of objects.
rows.anchor: فالاستثناء من أعم المفاعيل

rows.speaker: الشيخ المغربي
rows.claim: The Maghribi’s Persian couplet says that only the Beloved should be found in Mahmud’s heart.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ المغربي قدس سره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the surah presents—admonitions, promises and threats, and decisive proofs of divine oneness and prophethood—is sufficient for worshippers whose concern is worship rather than habit.
rows.anchor: من الأخبار والمواعظ البالغة والوعد والوعيد والبراهين القاطعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was sent with laws, rulings, and other foundations of happiness in both lives as mercy to all worlds; anyone who turns away brings hardship upon himself.
rows.anchor: بما ذكر وأمثاله من الشرائع والأحكام وغير ذلك من الأمور التي هي مناط السعادة في الدارين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the Prophet also showed mercy to unbelievers by postponing their punishment and sparing them collective destruction, being swallowed by the earth, or transformation.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : جاء رحمة للكفار أيضا

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: In a report, the Prophet asks Gabriel whether the mercy in this verse reached him; Gabriel says it did because he feared his fate until God praised him at 81:20–21.
rows.anchor: ورد في الخبر أنه عليه السلام قال لجبريل

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: Gabriel answers that the mercy reached him: he had feared the outcome until reassured by God’s praise of him as powerful, honored, obeyed, and trustworthy.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه السلام قال لجبريل : "إن الله يقول وما أرسلناك إلى آخره فهل أصابك من هذه الرحمة" قال : نعم

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi, citing Kashf al-Asrar, says the Prophet remembered his community at every station, including the Throne and the two-bows’ length, and will spread intercession at the Praiseworthy Station, crying for his community.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (در كشف الأسرار آورده كه از رحمت وى بودكه امت را در هي مقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian poem portrays sinners grasping the Prophet’s hem and relying on his intercession rather than despairing of his court.
rows.anchor: عاصيان ركنه در دامن آخر زمان دست درد امان تودارندو جان در آستين

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some spiritual masters call the Prophet’s mercy absolute, complete, universal, and encompassing every limited form of mercy; this universality entails his superiority to all worlds.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : وما أرسلناك إلا رحمة مطلقة تامة كاملة عامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct address is to the Prophet, while its inward indication extends to each heir who follows his path as a manifestation of his inheritance.
rows.anchor: خطاب للنبي عليه السلام فقط وإشارته خطاب لكل واحد من ورثته

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some spiritual masters say the Prophet is mercy to all worlds because he embodies magnificent character and gives each level—royal, spiritual, natural, psychic, spiritual, and secret—its due place.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الكبار : إنما كان رحمة للعالمين بسب اتصافه بالخلق العظيم

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya commentary contrasts Jesus’s partial mercy, limited by min and ending when his religion was abrogated, with Muhammad’s unrestricted mercy, which never ceases: his religion remains in this world and all creatures, even Abraham, need his intercession in the next.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" في سورة مريم

rows.speaker: عرائس البقلي
rows.claim: The Arāʾis al-Baqli says Muhammad’s light was the first creation; creatures from Throne to soil came from some of it, so his advent gives life and mercy to all existence.
rows.anchor: قال في "عرائس البقلى" : أيها الفهيم إن الله أخبرنا

rows.speaker: عرائس البقلي
rows.claim: All creatures were originally lifeless forms awaiting Muhammad; once he arrived, the world became alive because he is the spirit of all creatures.
rows.anchor: فإذا قدم إلى العالم صار العالم حيا بوجوده لأنه روح جميع الخلائق

rows.speaker: عرائس البقلي
rows.claim: Creatures could not know the mysteries of eternity or reach the shores of divine majesty, so Muhammad came as the elixir of bodies and spirit of forms, conveying primordial knowledge and clarifying the path of truth.
rows.anchor: لم يخرج من العدم إلا ناقصا من حيث الوقوف على أسرار قدمه بنعت كمال المعرفة والعلم

rows.speaker: عرائس البقلي
rows.claim: His journey compressed the beginning and end of time into one step, guiding all across the path of the Night Journey to the station of two bows’ length or nearer; by his blessed foot God forgave all creatures.
rows.anchor: بحيث جعل سفر الآزال والآباد للجميع خطوة واحدة فإذا قدم من الحضرة إلى سفر القربة

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars contrast earlier prophets as prelude to punishment, citing 17:15, with Muhammad as prelude to mercy; God made the last community’s beginning and end mercy, in keeping with the report that mercy precedes wrath.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العلماء : إن كل نبي كان مقدمة للعقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ahmadic reality emerged from the hidden divine presence when creation was willed, was marked with possibility, and became mercy and honor for humanity; spirits and then bodily forms flowed from it.
rows.anchor: أبرز الحقيقة الأحمدية من كمون الحضرة الأحدية فميزه بميم الامكان وجعله رحمة للعالمين وشرف به نوع الإنسان

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A saying attributed to the Prophet states that he is from God and believers are from the outpouring of his light.
rows.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام : "أنا من الله والمؤمنون من فيض نوري"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author presents Muhammad as the ultimate purpose in the ordering of created beginnings and cites the saying that the celestial spheres were created for his sake.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى : "لولاك لما خلقت الأفلاك"

rows.speaker: المولى الجامي
rows.claim: Jami’s couplet calls Muhammad the goal and joy of every realm and the intermediary through whom all existence comes.
rows.anchor: علت غائيه هر عالم اوست سرور اولاد بني آدم اوست واسطه فيض وجودي همه

rows.speaker: العرفي الشيرازي
rows.claim: ʿUrfi Shirazi’s praise poem says Muhammad’s honor lies in being the source of divine determination; the author reads ʿabathan reversed as baʿthan, resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال العرفي الشيرازي في قصيدته النعتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author infers that God created beings and sent messengers as preparation for Muhammad’s manifestation; their spirits and bodies follow his noble spirit and subtle body.
rows.anchor: يعني يكفيك شرفا وفضلا أن الله سبحانه إنما خلق الخلق وبعث الأنبياء والرسل ليكونوا مقدمة لظهورك

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet’s life and death are both mercy: the Companions ask how his death benefits them, and he says their deeds are shown to him twice weekly; he praises good and asks forgiveness for bad.
rows.anchor: حياته عليه السلام رحمة ومماته رحمة

rows.speaker: المولى الجامي
rows.claim: Jami’s poem asks the Prophet for compassion after his separation, saying he cannot leave the deprived without intercession if he is mercy to the worlds.
rows.anchor: قال المولى الجامي : زمهجورى برآمد جان عالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they turn from Islam and revelation, the Prophet must tell them he has warned them equally about the commanded affirmation of divine oneness and transcendence, withholding nothing and giving all equal counsel.
rows.anchor: أعرضوا عن الإسلام ولم يلتفتوا إلى ما يوجبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase on equal terms is circumstantial, describing the recipients of the warning.
rows.anchor: فهو حال من مفعول آذنتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet does not know whether the promised Muslim victory and establishment of religion, or the resurrection, is near or far, though punishment and humiliation will inevitably overtake them.
rows.anchor: من غلبة المسلمين وظهور الدين أو الحشر مع كونه آتيا لا محالة

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: Al-Asʾila al-Muqḥima asks how the timing can be unknown when 21:1 says the true promise has drawn near; the answer is that the Day of Resurrection is near, as that verse says.
rows.anchor: وفي "الأسئلة المقحمة" كيف قال هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows their public attacks on Islam and denial of revelations as well as concealed envy and hostility toward the Messenger and believers, and repays even the smallest amount; repeating the verb of knowing repeats the threat.
rows.anchor: ما تجاهرون به من الطعن في الإسلام وتكذيب الآيات {ويعلم ما تكتمون} من الحسد والعداوة للرسول وللمسلمين

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some spiritual masters say nothing about creation is hidden from God, who placed in bodies their qualities of good, evil, benefit, and harm; hidden and manifest are alike before him.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : كيف يخفي على الحق من الخلق خافية

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading says God knows public claims of Islam, faith, asceticism, piety, and gnosis, and what is concealed of sincerity, hypocrisy, ostentation, and reputation-seeking.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : {ويعلم ما تسرون وما تعلنون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delay of punishment may be called a trial because it is a form of gradual enticement that increases their testing and punishment, or it may test how they act by figurative comparison to an examination.
rows.anchor: لعل تأخير جزائكم {فتنة لكم} استدراج لكم وزيادة في افتنانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their enjoyment lasts until a divinely appointed term set by wise will, serving as evidence against them and bringing retribution at its proper time.
rows.anchor: وتمتيع لكم إلى أجل مقدر يقتضيه مشيئته المبنية على الحكم البالغة ليكون ذلك حجة عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet prays that God judge fairly between him and Mecca’s people, in a way that entails hastening punishment and severity for them.
rows.anchor: الرسول فهو حكاية لدعائه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rahman can mean abundant benefaction, an active attribute, or the will to convey good, an essential attribute.
rows.anchor: كثير الرحمة على عباده وهي إن كانت بمعنى الانعام فمن صفات الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mustaʿan is a second predicate and means the one from whom aid is sought against their assertions that Islam would fail and that a true warning would already have brought punishment.
rows.anchor: خبر آخر أي : المطلوب منه المعونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered the Messenger’s prayer, frustrated the Meccans’ hopes, changed their fortunes, and aided his allies at Badr.
rows.anchor: فاستجاب الله تعالى دعاء رسوله فخيب آمالهم وغير أحوالهم ونصر أولياءه عليهم فأصابهم يوم بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward lesson is that one should expect from God only what is due to the obedient or sinner under his primordial decree; his mercy remains infinite.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أنه لا يطلب من الله تعالى ولا يطمع في حق المطيع والعاصي إلا ما هو مستحقه

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that God has one hundred mercies, supporting the claim that divine mercy is limitless.
rows.anchor: على ما قال عليه السلام : "إنمائة رحمة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person should not be deceived by long life, wealth, or children; such complacency is characteristic of unbelievers.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن لا يغتر بطول العمر وكثرة الأموال والأولاد فإن الاغترار بذلك من صفات الكفرة

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين علي
rows.claim: Ali says that someone granted worldly abundance who fails to recognize it may be a divine ruse is deceived in intellect.
rows.anchor: ومن كلمات أمير المؤمنين علي رضي الله عنه : من وسع عليه دنياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For every community means all communities rather than only some members of each; the fronting gives a restrictive sense.
rows.anchor: من الأمم لا لبعض منهم دون بعض فالتقديم للتخصيص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mansak is a place or act of worship and a sacrifice used to draw near to God; here it means shedding blood for him.
rows.anchor: متعبدا وقربانا يتقربون به إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb nasaka yields forms meaning to slaughter a sacrifice; God prescribed that each believing community offer sacrifice to him.
rows.anchor: شرعنا لكل أمة مؤمنة أن ينسكوا له تعالى يقال نسك ينسك نسكا ونسوكا ومنسكا بفتح السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rites were instituted so that they remember God alone; remembrance of the worshipped is the primary aim of the rites.
rows.anchor: خاصة دون غيره ويجعلوا نسكهم لوجهه الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Specifying livestock after the word beast indicates that the offering must come from livestock; horses, mules, and donkeys do not qualify.
rows.anchor: في تبيين البهيمة بإضافتها إلى الأنعام تنبيه على أن القربان يجب أن يكون من الأنعام

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya inwardly maps each wayfarer’s path, station, and approach to God to their rank: some seek through works, striving, or God himself, and each remembers God through the granted conquest of the lower self and its animal traits, reaching stations and perfections.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : ولكل سالك جعلنا طريقة ومقاما وقربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa follows from the institution of rites: the one God cannot have a partner in essence or attributes, or the observed order of the world would collapse.
rows.anchor: الفاء لترتيب ما بعدها على ما قبلها من الجعل المذكور والخطاب للكل تغليبا أي فإلهكم إله منفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God is one, make the offering or remembrance sincerely for him alone and do not mix it with idolatry.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان إلهكم إله واحد فاجعلوا التقرب أو الذكر سالما له أي خالصا لوجهه ولا تشوبوه بالإشراك

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya commentary defines Islam here as sincerity: purifying deeds from flaws, morals from impurities, states from distraction, and breaths from all else.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : والإسلام يكون بمعنى الإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhbitin means the humble or sincere; because khabt is settled low ground, the settled person is metaphorically called humble and sincere.
rows.anchor: المتواضعين أو المخلصين فإن الخبت هو المطمئن من الأرض وحقيقة المخبت من صار في خبت الأرض

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi glosses the glad tidings as God’s boundless mercy to the humble.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (وبشارت ده أي محمد فروتنانرا

rows.speaker: سلمي قدس سره
rows.claim: Al-Sulami says the glad tidings are for longing seekers about the joy of seeing God, for nothing is more joy-giving.
rows.anchor: سلمي قدس سره فرمودهكه مزده ده مشتاقانرا بسعادت لقاكه هي مده ازين فرح آفزاي ترنيست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-budn is an accusative governed by an implied verb explained by what follows, as in 36:39; it is the plural of badana for camels and cattle used in offerings, named for their large bodies.
rows.anchor: منصوب بمضمر يفسره ما بعده كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Bahr al-ʿUlum says the word is linguistically for camels of either sex, but legally includes cattle because both are large-bodied; the Prophet therefore counted a cow as equivalent to a camel for one seventh share.
rows.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" : البدنة في اللغة من الإبل خاصة

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus defines badana as camel or cow, male or female, offered to Mecca like a sheep sacrifice.
rows.anchor: وفي "القاموس" : البدنة محركة من الإبل والبقر

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi translates the term as camels and cattle driven for the hady offering.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (وشتران وكاوان كه براي هدى رانده)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacrificial animals are among God’s religious signs; associating the signs with God magnifies them, since what is joined to the great is itself great.
rows.anchor: من أعلام دينه التي شرعها الله مفعول ثان للجعل ولكم ظرف لغو متعلق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The animals bring abundant worldly benefit and great reward in the next life.
rows.anchor: نفع كثير في الدنيا وأجر عظيم في العقبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishari lesson: sacrificing the animal-like lower self at the heart’s Kaʿba is a sign of faith and sincere seeking; its good lies in killing it with the knife of sincerity.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى قربان بهيمة النفس عند كعبة القلب وأنه من أعلام الدين وشعار أهل الصدق في الطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verse contrasts outward death with inward life and an outwardly broken form with hidden worth.
rows.anchor: ظاهرش مرك وبباطن زنده كي ظاهرش ابترنهان ايندكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At slaughter one says God is greatest, there is no deity but God, and God is greatest, then asks God, since the animal is his gift, to accept it as an approach to him.
rows.anchor: أي : هي عطاء منك ونتقرب بها إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawaff describes standing animals: camels stand with limbs aligned; the plural is of saffah, and their left forelegs are tied.
rows.anchor: كناية عن كونها قائمات لأن قيام الإبل يستلزم أن تصف أيديها وأرجلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that camels are slaughtered standing, with their left forelegs tied.
rows.anchor: والمعنى حال كونها قائمات قد صففن أيديهن وأرجلهن معقولة الأيدي اليسرى

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says standing the camel for slaughter is the Sunnah.
rows.anchor: كما قال الكاشفي : (صواف درحالتي كه براي ايستاده باشند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wajabat describes a wall falling; here the animal’s flanks falling to the ground is a metaphor for its death.
rows.anchor: يقال : وجب الحائط يجب وجبة إذا سقط

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi explains that when the slaughtered animals fall to earth, their souls leave them.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (س ون بيفتد برزمين هلو هاي مذبوحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eating from the sacrifice is permitted unless it is a liability offering, expiation, or vow offering; the command to eat is permissive.
rows.anchor: أي من لحومها أن لم يكن دم الجناية والكفارة والنذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feeding the poor is obligatory; the qaniʿ is content with what he has or receives without asking, while the muʿtarr comes seeking charity without explicitly asking.
rows.anchor: الأمر للوجوب {القانع} أي الراضي بما عنده وبما يعطى

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus defines muʿtarr as a poor person who approaches for charity without asking.
rows.anchor: كما قال في "القاموس" : المعتر الفقير المعترض للمعروف

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi cites Zad al-Masir for identifying the qaniʿ as a poor person of Mecca and the muʿtarr as a poor traveler from elsewhere.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (درزاد المسير آورده كه قانع فقير مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means God subjected the animals in this remarkable manner, as the description of them standing indicates.
rows.anchor: مثل ذلك التسخير البديع المفهوم من قوله صواف
